transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I've been feeling deeply depressed and down for a long time now. On top of that, I keep hearing voices and seeing things that other people tell me aren't actually there.
Do the voices or visions ever happen when you are not feeling depressed, or do they only happen during times when your depression is at its worst?

Yes, they actually do happen even when I'm not feeling depressed. There have been times, lasting at least a couple of weeks, where my mood was relatively okay but I still heard and saw things. It doesn't just happen when my depression is at its worst.

Over the whole time you’ve been ill, have your depressive episodes been present for most of the time that you’ve also had the voices or visions? Or have the psychotic symptoms been there for long stretches without much depression?

The depression has definitely been there for most of the time I've been dealing with all of this. However, there was a period of at least two weeks where I was still hearing and seeing things even though my mood felt relatively okay. But usually, they happen together.

The new information strengthens Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) because the patient reports depressive episodes present for most of the illness, along with at least a 2-week period of psychotic symptoms occurring when mood was relatively okay. Schizophrenia remains in the differential because chronic psychosis is present, but it is less favored if mood episodes have indeed occupied the majority of the total illness duration.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent psychotic symptoms (hearing voices and seeing things) along with longstanding depression. Critically, there was at least a two-week period of hallucinations occurring when mood was relatively okay, while depressive episodes have been present for most of the overall illness duration. This pattern supports Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) over Schizophrenia.
